sources.population: Taiwan Biobank 2012-2016 participants aged 30-70; 6184 men, 8353 women; genotype-selected analytic sample.
sources.measurement: HDL-C in mg/dL; BMI from biobank physical examination. Specific HDL assay and fasting protocol not stated in this article.
sources.cohort_overlap: No known overlap with the target. All evidence items from this paper share one cohort and are not independent confirmations.

sources.population: Urban Malawi MEIRU and UK ALSPAC adolescents and parents; adult analytic samples 2277 and 6323, respectively; adults mainly middle-aged.
sources.measurement: Fasting serum enzymatic lipids in Malawi (Beckman AU480); fasting plasma enzymatic lipids in UK (Technicon RA500); BMI measured.
sources.cohort_overlap: No known target overlap. The two countries are distinct cohorts. ALSPAC parent/child records can be related; not counted as independent replications.

sources.population: Dallas Heart Study probability sample, baseline 2000-2002; 1977 adults, 51% women, 46% Black; selected to exclude lipid therapy, hormone therapy, malignancy, connective tissue disease, HIV; survival at least one year.
sources.measurement: Fasting EDTA plasma; HDL-C reported in mg/dL separately from NMR HDL particles; specific cholesterol assay not fully stated.
sources.cohort_overlap: No known overlap with target, Taiwan Biobank or ALSPAC/MEIRU.

sources.population: Initial cross-sectional sample of 1065 Mexican mestizo adults ages 20-65, recruited in Mexico City, 2013-2018; excludes chronic disease, glucose >=6.93 mmol/L, smoking, alcohol, medications and several other conditions. Intervention samples are distinct subsets and are not used numerically.
sources.measurement: Overnight 12-hour fasting serum HDL measured on COBAS c111; BMI measured. This is not the target national sampling or assay protocol.
sources.cohort_overlap: No known target or other included-cohort overlap; cross-sectional and intervention parts of this paper are overlapping rather than independent evidence.

sources.population: 116 selected Turkish volunteers recruited with an endocrinology clinic; 10 obesity I, 13 obesity II, 22 obesity III. Extensive exclusions include chronic illness, diabetes/family history, hypertension, smoking, alcohol and regular extensive exercise. No sex mix by BMI group supplied.
sources.measurement: Overnight fasting blood collection; HDL-C reported in mg/dL; specific HDL assay is not supplied. Table 1 reports mean plus/minus SD.
sources.cohort_overlap: No known overlap with target or other included cohorts. Table 1 and Table 2 are one sample.

evidence.locator: Methods 2.2 and 2.4; Table 2, Sex rows; BMI columns underweight/normal/overweight/obese
evidence.estimand: Unadjusted arithmetic mean and standard error of HDL within sex by BMI category.
evidence.adjustment: None; each mean marginalizes the source age and unmeasured factors within its sex/BMI cell.
evidence.uncertainty: SEs explicitly identified in Methods and table, rounded to two decimals. Approximate individual cell SD = SE * sqrt(n); this is not regression residual SD.
evidence.applicability: Directly relevant predictor/outcome combination, but Taiwanese ethnicity, selection, ages 30-70 and unspecified assay limit U.S. transport.
evidence.model_use: Anchor sex-specific conditional location and scale curves using reported cell means and converted cell SDs.
bridge_assumptions: Place cell means at assumed BMI representatives rather than treating those representatives as observed means.
Use within-cell SD as a conditional SD proxy without fitting unavailable within-cell age/BMI distributions.
Transport the level/scale without an empirically estimated U.S. shift.

evidence.locator: Table 3, Age rows; Table 2, age stratum counts summed across BMI columns
evidence.estimand: Adjusted HDL arithmetic mean contrasts for age strata versus age 30-40.
evidence.adjustment: Multivariable model includes exercise, WHR, BMI category, body fat category, sex, smoking, drinking, coffee and vegetarian diet.
evidence.uncertainty: No confidence intervals or coefficient SEs in Table 3. The overlapping 40 label is a source labeling ambiguity; no participant recoding inferred.
evidence.applicability: Supplies modest cross-sectional age variation under a richer adjustment set, not a longitudinal aging effect or a sex-specific age slope.
evidence.model_use: Common piecewise linear age pattern, centered on source age-stratum weighted contrast.
bridge_assumptions: Treat category effects as point effects at approximate midpoints.
Use the same age pattern in both sexes and BMI groups; this is a parsimonious assumption, not evidence of no interaction.

evidence.estimand: Covariate-adjusted sex and BMI contrasts, including sex contrasts within BMI categories.
evidence.adjustment: Exercise, WHR, body fat, age, smoking, drinking, coffee, vegetarian diet; Table 5 stratified by BMI.
evidence.uncertainty: Table 5 p-values do not test a formal sex-by-BMI interaction; no coefficient covariance or CIs supplied.
evidence.applicability: Supports preserving sex differences and considering possible modification; adjusted BMI effects cannot replace marginal cell contrasts for the available predictor set.
evidence.model_use: Context for sex-specific curves; no second independent numerical weight or additional sex offset.
bridge_assumptions: Table 2 cell contrasts are used instead of stacking Table 3 adjusted effects onto them.

evidence.locator: Statistical analysis; Results paragraphs beginning The majority of the associations and Inverse associations; supplementary listing
evidence.estimand: Shape and population differences of age- and confounder-adjusted BMI-HDL associations.
evidence.adjustment: Initially age, then socioeconomic, behavioral, ethnicity and medication factors; HIV/physical activity in Malawi only.

reported.qualitative: Most associations linear; BMI-HDL inverse in each sex/age/country group; inverse BMI-HDL association stronger in UK; UK adult women stronger than men.
reported.numerical_supplement: Named supplement is PDF and gateway reports unsupported_supplement_format.

evidence.uncertainty: Exact HDL slopes and quintile locations unavailable through supported supplement route. Results also contain an apparent HDL/LDL labeling inconsistency in one positive adult-male example; that numeric example is not used.
evidence.applicability: Independent population comparison demonstrates imperfect transport and supplies no evidence for an exact high-BMI plateau.
evidence.model_use: Motivates declining rather than automatically flat extrapolation; qualitative support only.
bridge_assumptions: Neither qualitative linearity nor the unavailable supplement determines the high-BMI decay constant.

evidence.locator: Table 2, HDL-C Age rows; Methods standardized coefficient definition
evidence.estimand: Sex-specific standardized adjusted age coefficient in HDL-C regression.
evidence.adjustment: Sex-stratified model of age, ethnicity, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, insulin resistance, exercise, alcohol, log triglycerides, family history, CRP; menopause for women.
evidence.uncertainty: SD(age) and SD(HDL) needed for an unstandardized conversion are not supplied for these regression samples; R2 includes many unavailable predictors.
evidence.applicability: U.S. population, but selection and adjustment differ substantially. Counters universal common-age assumptions.
evidence.model_use: Age-by-sex remains an important gap; do not use beta as mg/dL/year or treat non-significant male beta as known zero.

evidence.estimand: Sex/ethnicity-specific marginal median and interquartile range of HDL-C.
evidence.uncertainty: Quantiles, not means or standard deviations; sampling uncertainty not stated.
evidence.applicability: Marginal variability broadly contextualizes the model but joint BMI and age distributions are unavailable.
evidence.model_use: Transport and scale context; no pooled target calibration.
bridge_assumptions: Cannot match source marginals without corresponding source predictor/ethnicity distributions.

evidence.locator: Table 5 Age rows, compared with Table 3; Table 2 Age rows supply stratum counts.
evidence.estimand: Adjusted within-BMI-category HDL mean differences by age category versus age 30-40.
evidence.adjustment: Separate regression by BMI category, including exercise, WHR, body fat, sex, smoking, drinking, coffee and vegetarian diet. Thus not merely BMI/age/sex conditioning.
evidence.uncertainty: No formal age-by-BMI interaction test, coefficient covariance or SEs. Largest point differences occur in underweight stratum with n=408, including n=45 at age 61-70. Separate p-values do not establish interaction.
evidence.applicability: Same source as main anchors, but residual adjustment and source cell mixing still differ from available target predictors. Does not supply age-by-sex estimates.
evidence.model_use: Added direct age-modification sensitivity. Retained pooled Table 3 age curve in selected generator; no numerical model change.
bridge_assumptions: Age knots and category means are distinct from individual conditional effects.
The finite common-versus-stratified contrast comparison is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a probability interval or a formal interaction estimate.

evidence.locator: Participants, Biochemical Parameters, Results cross-sectional section, Figure 1 caption, and supporting-information description of Table S1.
evidence.estimand: Sex-specific HDL comparison across normal/overweight/obesity I-II-III categories in selected Mexican adults.
evidence.adjustment: Descriptive comparisons; one-/two-way ANOVA mentioned; extensive participant selection. Not target-compatible fully adjusted conditional model.

reported.description: Obese participants had lower HDL in both sexes than normal-weight participants; the named Table S1 contains sex-by-obesity-class anthropometric/biochemical summaries.
reported.availability: Table S1 is within JAH3-8-e012401-s001.pdf; gateway lists unsupported_supplement_format; contents not accessed.

evidence.uncertainty: Exact sex/class means and uncertainty unavailable through supported route; do not digitize unrequested figure pixels or infer missing numbers.
evidence.applicability: Broad obesity categories and a COBAS serum measure are relevant leads; selected, largely overweight/obese Mexican sample has different exclusions and population.
evidence.model_use: Context and documented failed quantitative lead; no numerical calibration.

evidence.locator: Methods group definitions and n; Table 1, obese class I, II, III rows and table footnote.
evidence.estimand: Unadjusted HDL-C mean and SD in three obesity classes; corresponding BMI and age means.
evidence.adjustment: None. Groups not matched, sex mix per category unavailable.
evidence.uncertainty: Small selected groups, no sex stratification or within-group predictor/outcome covariance. Published p-values compare each group to normal-weight, not within-obesity contrasts; no inferential weight assigned. Other discussion/reference-derived numerical claims are not used.
evidence.applicability: Primary within-obesity means provide a concrete declining-shape example through mean BMI 45.77. They do not establish target conditional sex-specific decline or behavior up to BMI 77.5.
evidence.model_use: Source-scale contrast of class III minus I (-5.24 mg/dL) computed and compared descriptively with the selected and flat-tail alternatives at reported BMI means; tail parameters retained.
bridge_assumptions: Plug-in predictions at group mean BMI/age are not integrated source predictions because of nonlinearity and missing sex/joint distributions.
Source contrast does not identify the selected asymptotes or decay parameter; it only keeps continuing decline plausible.
